name: Sittalai Sattanar
bio: Sittalai Sattanar (சீத்தலைச் சாத்தனார்) is the traditional author of the Manimekalai, the Buddhist epic of Tamil. Tradition calls him a grain merchant of Madurai; the name "Sittalai" ("scarred head") is said to come from a habit of striking his head with his stylus when he found a poem faulty. He is known otherwise only through the epic itself and a few poems attributed to the name in the Sangam anthologies, and his date is debated, the sixth century CE being a common estimate.

The Manimekalai ("The Jewelled Girdle") is the twin of Ilango Adigal's Silappatikaram and continues its story: Manimekalai, the daughter of Kovalan and the dancer Madhavi, renounces the world and becomes a Buddhist nun. The poem is in thirty cantos (kathais) with a prologue, in the akaval metre, and is a major source for early Buddhist thought and for city life in the Tamil country.
